name: Chris Anders
life: “I still remember counting bus coins with oily thumbs.” Thursday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Chris knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I was sure my envelope had been opened. The crease was mine from the night I nearly spent it.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an old plum windbreaker and a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. Chris has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Chris takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Chris has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Chris knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To clear the accusation over the opened envelope.
family: Bianca Cole is Chris’s cousin. Chris chooses the music. Bianca puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Five missing lunches*, Bianca says, “I was asked to throw them away. I put a forwarding card in each one instead.”
connections: Lola Lowe. The deli-table count gives the worried owner a chance to recognize a familiar crease.

reactions.response: Chris asks each renter how much of the count they want heard in public.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Chris accepts a small agreed amount if paying lets the neighbor keep their pride.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Chris asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
